records.program_name: Computer Science Major, BS in Computer Science
records.college: Tickle College of Engineering (Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science)
records.grade_requirements: At least a C in every computer engineering, computer science, electrical engineering and mathematics course used for the degree.
records.progression: Progression to upper-division departmental programs is competitive and space-limited; factors include overall GPA, grades in required lower-division courses, and orderly progress without abuse of withdrawal/repeat privileges.
records.utrack: Full-time degree-seeking students must meet uTrack milestones in terms 1-5 (e.g., term 1: MATH 130/131 or higher; terms 3-4: engineering physics sequence; term 5: one listed intro course).

electives: Volunteer Core elective (AH, GCUS, GCI or SS) per term listing

courses: Science option (BIOL 101/104/150, PHYS 231, CHEM 128, or CHEM 102+103 / CHEM 122+123)
ECE 313 or ECE 317 or STAT 251 or MATH 323

records.upper_division_electives_rule: Any 3XX/4XX COSC or ECE course not otherwise used, MATH 231, 241, 371, 471, 472; up to three COSC/ECE 5XX courses; COSC 322 does not count.
records.engaged_inquiries_rule: Minimum of 9 credit hours in at least two subject areas.
records.prior_credit_notes: AP Computer Science A score of 3+ earns COSC 101; a departmental proficiency exam for COSC 101 is available on request.
records.honors_concentration: Overall 3.4 GPA, four 100/200-level honors courses (14+ hours), two upper-division COSC/ECE honors courses and Cook Grand Challenge breadth requirements.
records.five_year_bs_ms: Up to 9 graduate hours count toward both degrees; 3.4 GPA; conditional admission after 64 hours, full admission after 96 hours.
records.notes: Term 1 in the catalog lists COSC 103/104 while the footnote still references COSC 101/102; reproduced as printed. University-wide bachelor's requirements (120 hours, 30 upper-division, residence rules) apply in addition. Elective term placement is the catalog's suggested sequence, not a hard requirement.
